 PALM BEACH COUNTY, Fla. (CBS12) — A 3-year-old was in the truck as her father allegedly continued driving after troopers activated their lights and sirens during a stop on I-95 near Boynton Beach, according to a Florida Highway Patrol arrest report.
 The report identifies the driver as Jeremiah Baxter, 29. It says troopers responded after the Lake Worth Regional Communications Center relayed a caller’s report that a black Dodge Ram was swerving, traveling without headlights and being driven by someone who appeared to be drinking and using a phone.
 A trooper saw the truck traveling north without headlights or taillights and following another vehicle too closely, the report says. After the trooper activated the patrol car’s lights and siren, Baxter continued driving at about 40 mph in a 65-mph zone, eventually moving onto the shoulder. He continued after a trooper used a public address speaker to order him to stop, according to the report.
 See also: Florida education department says data breach may affect 4.9 million people 
 A second trooper moved in front of the truck, and Baxter stopped. The first trooper drew a firearm and repeatedly ordered Baxter to show his hands, the report says. Troopers allege Baxter refused commands to show his hands and get out of the truck, then resisted as they removed and handcuffed him.
 Baxter shouted that his daughter was in the truck. Troopers confirmed the 3-year-old was in a car seat in the rear passenger-side seat. The child’s mother arrived and took custody of her, the report says.
 During an inventory search, troopers say they found two bags containing a total of 2.7 grams of marijuana in a backpack, along with pre-rolled tips. Field tests were positive for marijuana. No alcoholic beverages were found in the truck. The trooper reported a slight odor of alcohol on Baxter’s breath but said there were no other signs of impairment and did not pursue a DUI case.
 Baxter told troopers he had not been drinking. He said he delayed stopping because he was on the phone and adjusting a neck pillow around his daughter, according to the report.
 Baxter was booked into the Palm Beach County Jail. He faces four misdemeanor charges: failure to obey a lawful order, resisting an officer without violence, possession of less than 20 grams of marijuana, and possession of drug paraphernalia. He also received a civil traffic citation for driving at night without headlights or taillights.
